The Supreme Court says New Hampshire election officials are no longer allowed to consider
student IDs at all when verifying voters' identity for the midterm elections.
And Pierre's Hansi Lo Wang reports.
The Supreme Court ruling means that a student voter in New Hampshire must continue to show
at the polls a state ID, U.S. passport, or another accepted proof of their identity that
isn't a student ID. The unsigned order by the high court is part of an early stage of
a legal fight over one of the latest laws in Republican-led states that ban registered
voters from checking in at the polls with their student IDs. There are also lawsuits
over Indiana's ban, as well as a Florida ban that's set to start next year.
Challengers argue these bans violate the U.S. Constitution by making it harder for eligible
students to vote. Republican state officials claim these bans support election security.
But there is no evidence of widespread voter fraud involving student IDs.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
The president of El Salvador has launched a military operation in Haiti. NPR's Eder Peralta
reports they're trying to recover Salvadoran hostages.
The Salvadoran military announced that on Sunday, four Salvadoran aviation techs were
ambushed and taken hostage by heavily armed Haitian gangs. The Salvadorans deployed helicopters,
which they say were also attacked. On Wednesday, Salvadoran President Naib Bukele announced
what he called a military operation. He released a video showing armored vehicles moving through
Port-au-Prince. And he issued a warning, writing, quote, "Today's attack is nothing compared
to what is coming if we do not get all four hostages back alive." The Haitian government
said recovering the Salvadorans was an absolute priority. No one has claimed responsibility
for the attack. Eder Peralta, NPR News, Mexico City.
Mark Zuckerberg has made a deal with META to help him pay a proposed billionaire tax
that's on the ballot in California. Proposition 40 would levy a one-time 5 percent tax on
the wealth of Californians, whose net worth exceeds $1 billion. Supporters say it would
help ensure the ultra-rich pay their fair share, but opponents warn it could prompt
the state's wealthiest to leave the state.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is helping significantly reduce the chances that melanoma
tumors return, according to drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-made for
each patient. It teaches the immune system to watch out for and attack any cancer cells
that start forming again, adding it to the standard treatment reduced by 42 percent,
the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery. Astronomers think they have a new
date for when Vincent van Gogh painted his famous canvas "The Starry Night." As NPR's
Jeff Brumfield reports, it's a month later than previously believed.
Astronomers use simulations to nail down the exact date they think "The Starry Night"
represents, July 22, 1889. The researchers from Kyunghee University in South Korea say
the stars, the moon, and the planet Venus line up in a way that suggests it was paced
on their positions in the early morning. Conventional wisdom has that "The Starry Night"
was painted in June. That's in part based on Letter van Gogh himself wrote, in which
he discussed painting a new study of "The Starry Sky" around that time. The researchers
say their results are not conclusive, but they argued the date the famous painting was
created should be reconsidered in light of their analysis. The work appears in the journal
Scientific Reports. Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
The New York City Council passed a bill today that would ban horse carriage rides in the
city by June, 2028. It'll end a tradition beloved by tourists but long opposed by animal
welfare activists. The death of a tourist spurred the latest push to end the rides.
Drivers say they're being forced out of jobs unfairly. This is NPR News.
